chart_rows.baseline_name: geometry ExtraTrees reference

chart_rows.description: This solution classifies mouse social behavior from pose using hand-crafted features extracted from the context window for each frame, followed by a gradient boosting classifier. The features include within-frame and across-window statistics of inter-animal distances, within-animal body part distances (e.g., nose-to-neck), displacement and velocity features based on position differences across time offsets, and relative orientation angles between keypoints. The model employs scikit-learn's HistGradientBoostingClassifier for efficient training and robust generalization, and the code sets numpy RNG and model seeds to ensure determinism. Cross-validation is done via five-fold stratified split on the training set to select the best model configuration (using macro-F1 score); however, due to constraints, hyperparameter tuning is light and deterministic. The entire pipeline keeps memory usage and runtime suitable for a single CPU. Output is the integer label per test sample, matching the input shape.

Train a deterministic classifier on engineered spatiotemporal pose features without any cross-example smoothing. For each sample (already containing the 7 temporal offsets at [-15,-5,-1,0,1,5,15]) we build translation- and scale-robust features from the two animals’ keypoints: distances (nose–nose, center–center, and minimum landmark distance across animals) at each offset; instantaneous separation change and approach speeds over ±1/±5/±15; individual nose speeds; head/body orientation cosines and their alignment with the inter-animal axis; head turning (cosine of angle change) over ±1 and ±5; intra-animal shape features normalized by body length (ear gap, hip gap, neck–tail, nose–tail, nose–to–center) for each animal; and several pair-centric projections (e.g., longitudinal offsets). Distances are normalized by the geometric mean of both animals’ body lengths at t=0. Inputs with NaN/inf are imputed per example using the mean across its 7 offsets (fallback to 0 if all NaN). A single HistGradientBoostingClassifier (no early stopping; fixed random seed) is trained on all training data with class-balanced sample weights (inverse-frequency). Predictions are class argmax for each target frame. No features are computed across example boundaries and no temporal smoothing of outputs is performed.

chart_rows.baseline_name: temporal linear interpolation
chart_rows.description: Deterministic motion-capture-only reconstruction. It blends linear, Cartesian cubic-spline, and body-frame cubic-spline interpolation, then learns a rotation/translation-equivariant ridge correction from observed head context, visible spine motion, and local frame rotations. A deterministic final-fifth holdout selects the interpolation strategy, ridge penalty, and correction shrinkage; selected settings are refit on all training windows. Outputs preserve observed test values and fill only missing HeadF coordinates in native mocap units.

chart_rows.baseline_name: temporal linear interpolation
chart_rows.description: Blend smooth interpolation in world, body, and transported head coordinates, including rigid head geometry. A regularized nonlinear residual model uses visible motion to refine the gap. A deterministic training-only holdout selects interpolation weights, regularization, and correction strength; the residual model is then refit using all eligible training windows. Observed test values are preserved, and predictions remain in native motion-capture coordinates.

chart_rows.baseline_name: temporal linear interpolation
temporal linear interpolation
chart_rows.description: This method imputes missing 7-frame interior gaps of HeadF xyz landmarks in rat 3D motion-capture windows using a non-iterative K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) regression approach, fitted per HeadF coordinate. For each of the 7 masked frames (window indices 12:19), a separate KNN regressor is trained using valid frames from the training set (excluding masked test animal indices, leveraging only animals 1–3 from training). The regressors predict HeadF's missing values based on the 15 other fully-observed features (all non-HeadF landmark xyz positions at the same timepoint), using the corresponding features in test windows. The approach is fully offline and acausal, making predictions for masked frames solely from their observed coordinates. Predictions are reassembled into the original test_x shape with only the masked locations replaced, ensuring finite values at those locations and strict separation of animals by dataset split. The number of neighbors is fixed (k=5), and regression is non-weighted for simplicity; training points with NaNs in predictors or targets are excluded. The method is deterministic, using no random processes. No temporal dynamics or sequence modeling is invoked; the prediction leverages only spatial geometric context at each imputation frame. No browsing or file I/O occurs. All computation fits in a single fit_predict function, conforming to time and memory constraints.

chart_rows.baseline_name: temporal linear interpolation
chart_rows.description: Gap imputation for HeadF (x,y,z) over frames 12–18 using a two-step method. 1) Per-window acausal linear interpolation baseline anchored at the two observed endpoints (frames 11 and 19). 2) Learn a residual correction from observed context using ridge regression trained on animals 1–3 (train_x -> train_y). For each missing frame t, features include: other 5 landmarks (15 dims) at t±2..t±0 (75 dims), the baseline HeadF at t (3), the two HeadF endpoints (6), and timing features within-gap and absolute frame index (2); total 86 features. We train a single multi-target closed-form ridge (no randomness) on residuals (y_true − baseline) for the three HeadF coordinates jointly, with feature standardization and no penalty on the intercept. At test time (animals 4–5), we compute the same features and add predicted residuals to the linear baseline, then write back only the masked HeadF frames; all other coordinates/timepoints are left unchanged. Windows are treated independently and no temporal stitching across windows is performed. Hyperparameters fixed (alpha=1.0); no cross-validation; deterministic linear algebra only.

Fixed log-spectral-feature HistGradientBoosting; every fifth whole training recording validates global threshold/gap/minimum duration, then refit all training recordings; no bird IDs or pretrained weights
chart_rows.description: Fit a scipy+sklearn pipeline for supervised binary (event) detection in 1ms frames, trained on annotated Bengalese finch audio. The feature pipeline computes log-mel-like band energies from the STFT, noise-floor normalizes per recording, then augments with broadband power and temporal smoothing. chart_rows.description: Deterministic, fully unsupervised sorter. It common-median references the recording, estimates per-channel noise with robust MAD statistics, detects negative spatiotemporal peaks with geometry-aware nonmaximum suppression, and extracts aligned multichannel snippets. Waveform PCA, estimated source location, and amplitude features are clustered by diagonal Gaussian mixtures; component count is selected using BIC on the supplied recording. Highly similar or coincident components are merged, while low-support, weak, edge-dominated, or temporally unstable templates are rejected. Final within-unit refractory deduplication prevents duplicate events. Validation uses only internal template stability, morphology, support, and refractory consistency—never hidden labels, a prescribed unit count, or external templates.

Unsupervised spatial whitening, local spike detection, waveform PCA and overclustering with projection-based mode merging. Robust templates drive iterative matching and whole-recording refinement. Unit counts come from voltage-derived clusters; no labels, external templates, or claimed benchmark score are used.

This is a baseline unsupervised neuroscience spike sorting algorithm for multi-channel extracellular recordings. This pipeline uses threshold-based event detection, waveform extraction via local maxima, channel whitening (pre-whitening), PCA-based dimensionality reduction, and clustering using HDBSCAN to automatically infer the number of units. Each detected event is reduced to a contiguous snippet around its peak, projected to PCA space, and clustered. Each event is labeled with the corresponding cluster (unit) assignment and its sample index. No ground-truth labels, simulated templates, or unit counts are used. The process is fully unsupervised, deterministic (fixed random seeds), and based strictly on provided voltage data. No units are artificially created or aligned to hidden ground-truth counts. The main steps are: (1) detect candidate spikes using a global (multi-channel) threshold; (2) extract windowed multi-channel snippets around peaks; (3) pre-whiten snippets; (4) reduce dimensionality by PCA (using a fixed number of components); (5) cluster PCA-projected snippets using HDBSCAN; (6) output spike sample indices and integer cluster/unit IDs, sorted by time, then unit ID. Event duplicate suppression enforces min refractory. Multiple parameters can be tuned for detection and snippet size, but defaults are chosen for general recordings. The output is a NumPy array (n_events, 2), with sample index and unit ID. No extra output or file/network use.

Unsupervised, single-shot spike sorting for a 32-channel, 10 s extracellular recording. Steps:
- Common-average referencing (subtract per-sample median across channels) and robust per-channel noise estimation via MAD to get sigma.
- Negative threshold detection on each channel using robust threshold (4.5·sigma), local-minimum selection with per-channel refractory (12 samples ≈ 0.375 ms).
- Cross-channel deduplication: merge candidate peaks within ±12 samples across all channels, keep the most negative trough as a single event and record its primary channel and amplitude.
- Discard events too close to recording edges for waveform extraction.
- Geometry-aware feature extraction: for each event, take 8 nearest channels by electrode geometry, extract 48-sample snippets (0.5 ms pre, 1.0 ms post), whiten by per-channel sigma, flatten, and compute low-dimensional features using PCA (8 components) learned on an evenly spaced subset (up to 5000 events). Concatenate a normalized amplitude feature.
- Robust feature scaling (median/MAD) and clustering with KMeans using a heuristic K (3–16 depending on spike count). Discard tiny clusters.
- Template merging: build per-cluster mean templates across all 32 channels from up to 150 events/cluster (whitened). Merge clusters whose template cosine similarity > 0.95 and with primary channels within 65 µm (union-find).
- Enforce intra-unit refractory: within each unit, allow at most one spike per 12 samples, keeping the more negative amplitude event.
- Return integer array [sample_index, unit_id], sorted by sample then unit, with contiguous nonnegative unit IDs. No supervision, deterministic seeds, no ground-truth use.
Validation policy: purely unsupervised on the full 10 s recording; no use of any hidden labels/true unit counts/templates. Parameters chosen conservatively for generality and speed on a single CPU thread. No duplicate events within a unit are emitted; empty output is valid if no spikes are detected.

latest_successes.description:
Unsupervised, single-shot spike sorting for a 32-channel, 10 s extracellular recording. Steps:
- Common-average referencing (subtract per-sample median across channels) and robust per-channel noise estimation via MAD to get sigma.
- Negative threshold detection on each channel using robust threshold (4.5·sigma), local-minimum selection with per-channel refractory (12 samples ≈ 0.375 ms).
- Cross-channel deduplication: merge candidate peaks within ±12 samples across all channels, keep the most negative trough as a single event and record its primary channel and amplitude.
- Discard events too close to recording edges for waveform extraction.
- Geometry-aware feature extraction: for each event, take 8 nearest channels by electrode geometry, extract 48-sample snippets (0.5 ms pre, 1.0 ms post), whiten by per-channel sigma, flatten, and compute low-dimensional features using PCA (8 components) learned on an evenly spaced subset (up to 5000 events). Concatenate a normalized amplitude feature.
- Robust feature scaling (median/MAD) and clustering with KMeans using a heuristic K (3–16 depending on spike count). Discard tiny clusters.
- Template merging: build per-cluster mean templates across all 32 channels from up to 150 events/cluster (whitened). Merge clusters whose template cosine similarity > 0.95 and with primary channels within 65 µm (union-find).
- Enforce intra-unit refractory: within each unit, allow at most one spike per 12 samples, keeping the more negative amplitude event.
- Return integer array [sample_index, unit_id], sorted by sample then unit, with contiguous nonnegative unit IDs. No supervision, deterministic seeds, no ground-truth use.
Validation policy: purely unsupervised on the full 10 s recording; no use of any hidden labels/true unit counts/templates. Parameters chosen conservatively for generality and speed on a single CPU thread. No duplicate events within a unit are emitted; empty output is valid if no spikes are detected.

chart_rows.description: General numerical strategy for B03 rigid-motion prediction from detected-peak spatial temporal raster: Estimate recording displacement time-series for each test simulation, using only training data for parameter selection and never accessing true test targets. The method builds on the principle that rigid axial displacements cause column-wide translations in detected-peak distributions, visible as depth shifts in the raster. We extract a depth activation profile for each second, then measure per-bin shifts using cross-correlation across time. Without knowledge of any fixed spatial reference, we treat the mean depth distribution for each recording as a moving template and track displacement as the best-aligned shift relative to this template. We apply robust normalization and parabolic refinement for sub-bin precision. The temporal mean is subtracted per recording. No training target access, fit to test data, or SI code is used; only sklearn, numpy, scipy are imported. One consistent random seed; test simulations processed independently. The entire fit_predict code below is stand-alone and self-contained.

chart_rows.baseline_name: SpikeInterface0.105.4 decentralized pairwise raster registration + global LSMR, fixed parameters
chart_rows.description:
Deterministic, training-calibrated rigid-motion inference from depth–time peak-count rasters.

Core idea
- For each 1 s time bin, z-score the 132-bin depth profile (zero-mean across depth, unit variance).
- For every pair of time bins (i<j), compute the normalized cross-correlation over integer spatial shifts within ±60 μm (±12 bins). The best shift s_ij and its correlation c_ij give a relative displacement measurement: x_j - x_i ≈ s_ij·5 μm.
- Keep only reliable edges with c_ij ≥ 0.1. Weight each edge by (c_ij - 0.1) and a temporal proximity decay exp(-|i-j|/τ).
- Solve a global least-squares problem over all time bins to find displacements x_t that fit the pairwise constraints while being temporally smooth: minimize Σ_e w_e^2(x_j - x_i - d_e)^2 + λ Σ_t (x_t - x_{t-1})^2. A small anchor on x_0 removes the null gauge; the scorer later subtracts the mean per recording.

Training
- Build edges on each of the 4 training recordings (no label leakage).
- Grid-search τ ∈ {8,12,18,30,45,60} s and λ ∈ {0.001,0.003,0.01,0.03,0.1,0.3,1,3}; for each pair, solve all 4 recordings and select the combination minimizing average RMSE versus mean-removed train_y.

Prediction
- For each test recording, rebuild edges from its raster only (no cross-record borrowing) and solve once with the trained (τ,λ). Return the raw x (any constant offset is allowed; scorer mean-centers).

Computational notes
- Depth-bin size is 5 μm, so shifts are integer bins. Normalized cross-correlations are computed per pair with proper overlap normalization and a minimal overlap of 40 bins to stabilize scores.
- The global system is solved via a dense 90×90 linear system (normal equations). λ is scaled by the ratio trace(M)/trace(L) for stability across recordings.
- Deterministic, no randomized operations. Uses only NumPy and math. Fits the 180 s/1-thread/4 GB constraints comfortably.

chart_rows.description: Lossless adaptive codec using per-channel centering, quantized AR(2) prediction, reversible cross-channel prediction, zigzag mapping, byte-plane transposition, and size-based selection between LZMA and BZ2. All prediction metadata is embedded in the compressed blob.
Lossless integer temporal and spatial prediction, followed by block-adaptive entropy models, rANS coding, and packed residual bits. All fitted parameters are included in the blob.

This codec compresses Neuropixels voltage recordings (C-contiguous int16 arrays, shape (4096,384), dtype '<i2') losslessly and decodes them exactly. Compression uses a two-stage process: 1) a simple predictive coding step (per-channel delta, i.e., storing differences along time for each channel), followed by 2) standard entropy compression (zlib, bz2, or lzma) selected for best compression per-chunk. The first row of each channel is stored verbatim for reconstruction. The compressed blob stores a header with a mode selector and all necessary metadata for decoding. Decompression uses the shape/dtype arguments and the header to restore the original array exactly. No cross-chunk state, external source info, or learning is used. All prediction and compression steps use reproducible, deterministic logic. The output blob size is minimized while satisfying exact reconstruction requirements.

Lossless codec for Neuropixels int16 (little-endian) data shaped (time, channels). It uses fast, fully reversible integer transforms tailored to spatiotemporal correlations, then strong entropy coding:
- Temporal first-order differencing per channel (along rows/time).
- Spatial first-order differencing across channels (along columns).
- ZigZag mapping of signed 16-bit residuals to unsigned 16-bit magnitudes.
- Byte shuffling (all low bytes first, then all high bytes) to expose long runs of 0x00/0xFF for better compression.
- LZMA compression (preset=6) with a tiny header.
Decoding reverses: LZMA decompress → unshuffle bytes → inverse ZigZag → prefix sums across channels → prefix sums across time. All arithmetic is exact under 16-bit two’s-complement wrap-around by using 32-bit accumulators and final casting. No external metadata beyond provided shape/dtype is used. Deterministic, fast, and memory-efficient, while typically achieving strong compression on neural voltage traces.

A lossy compression scheme for globally time-sorted float64 event times (sec) and int32 labels, optimized for sub-50μs precision and mean bits/event. Timestamps are delta-encoded at 10μs quantization, then packed as unsigned varints for size efficiency. Labels are stored as int32s. All data is streamed with headers, and compressed with zlib at max compression. Decompression unpacks and reconstructs approximate event times and exact labels. No dynamic state or file access; all standard Python3/NumPy/struct/zlib; deterministic output via seeded shuffling is not required. Meets B08 contract under specified constraints.

Spike-event compressor/decompressor for task B08. Times are quantized onto a fixed 50 µs grid via monotone floor, guaranteeing nondecreasing decoded times and absolute timing error < 50 µs. The pipeline:
- Quantize times: tick = floor(t / 5e-5) with a small positive bias to avoid boundary underflow.
- Encode ticks: store first tick as signed varint (zigzag), then unsigned varint deltas for subsequent ticks.
- Encode labels: build a palette of sorted unique int32 labels, encode the palette using delta + zigzag varints, and store per-event palette indices as a compact fixed-width byte array (1/2/4 bytes depending on palette size).
- The whole payload is LZMA (XZ) compressed. Decoder uses only the blob and shared code constants; no external state. Labels are exact and order preserved; times are nondecreasing with error bound met. Implementation stays under resource limits and uses deterministic behavior.

chart_rows.description: This method fits a simple parametric nonnegative deconvolution model, separately for each train neuron, to approximate spike rates from the calcium trace. For each train neuron, we use non-negative least squares (scipy.optimize.nnls) to learn a calcium→spike kernel of configurable lag (default 6 lags, 0.06 s). This is equivalent to fitting a temporal convolution kernel that predicts spike rate from past fluorescence. After removing trailing NaNs, the kernel is fit on each train neuron's available data, with optional z-scoring for fluorescence and spikes to handle scale differences. For test neurons, we standardize using their own mean and std (ignoring NaNs), and for each test neuron we select the train neuron (kernel) whose fit on held-out train data best matches the test neuron's own calcium standard deviation (and number of available samples). The selected kernel is convolved with the test fluorescence (acausally, as the function is run offline) and predictions are re-centered and rescaled as needed. Negative values are set to zero, and original NaNs are retained. Prediction shape matches test_calcium. All code is vectorized across time. No cross-neuron mixing occurs in any step.

Global linear deconvolution via Wiener filter learned from training neurons. We robustly standardize each train trace (median/MAD), compute aggregated auto-correlation of calcium and cross-correlation with spikes using FFT-based convolution, then solve a ridge-regularized Toeplitz normal equation to obtain a single two-sided FIR filter (acausal and causal lags ±0.8 s at 100 Hz). For test neurons, we robustly standardize each trace, apply the learned two-sided filter via efficient lagged additions, and rectify to enforce nonnegativity. Trailing NaNs in inputs remain NaN in outputs; predictions are finite where inputs are finite. No mixing across neuron boundaries or use of test labels. The method is simple, fast, and scale/offset agnostic (correlation metric is scale-invariant).

chart_rows.description: This method fits a simple parametric nonnegative deconvolution model, separately for each train neuron, to approximate spike rates from the calcium trace. For each train neuron, we use non-negative least squares (scipy.optimize.nnls) to learn a calcium→spike kernel of configurable lag (default 6 lags, 0.06 s). This is equivalent to fitting a temporal convolution kernel that predicts spike rate from past fluorescence. After removing trailing NaNs, the kernel is fit on each train neuron's available data, with optional z-scoring for fluorescence and spikes to handle scale differences. For test neurons, we standardize using their own mean and std (ignoring NaNs), and for each test neuron we select the train neuron (kernel) whose fit on held-out train data best matches the test neuron's own calcium standard deviation (and number of available samples). The selected kernel is convolved with the test fluorescence (acausally, as the function is run offline) and predictions are re-centered and rescaled as needed. Negative values are set to zero, and original NaNs are retained. Prediction shape matches test_calcium. All code is vectorized across time. No cross-neuron mixing occurs in any step.

Global linear deconvolution via Wiener filter learned from training neurons. We robustly standardize each train trace (median/MAD), compute aggregated auto-correlation of calcium and cross-correlation with spikes using FFT-based convolution, then solve a ridge-regularized Toeplitz normal equation to obtain a single two-sided FIR filter (acausal and causal lags ±0.8 s at 100 Hz). For test neurons, we robustly standardize each trace, apply the learned two-sided filter via efficient lagged additions, and rectify to enforce nonnegativity. Trailing NaNs in inputs remain NaN in outputs; predictions are finite where inputs are finite. No mixing across neuron boundaries or use of test labels. The method is simple, fast, and scale/offset agnostic (correlation metric is scale-invariant).

latest_successes.description: This procedure implements single-shot, group-aware, specimen-held-out spike rate inference for OGB-1 zebrafish data. It performs group-k-fold cross-validation on training specimens, trains a pipeline on full training data, and predicts for held-out test animals. Each input recording is handled independently; no resampling, no cross-record smoothing. The method constructs a compact sequence of steps: per-record Z-score normalization (mask-aware), extraction of per-record statistics, linear regression with group-k-fold cross-validation grouped by train specimen, and a nonnegativity constraint enforced post-prediction. Padding/invalid frames (channel 1 mask == 0) are handled carefully: normalization, model fitting and loss computation are restricted to valid frames; training targets with value -1 are excluded. Standard errors are returned for every step. Deterministic seed ensures fixed splits and reproducibility.
latest_successes.patch_description: Materialize the original GroupKFold splits using provided training groups; clip roundoff-negative rolling variances before sqrt. No label/test feedback or estimator replacement.

chart_rows.baseline_name: Conventional task baseline
chart_rows.description: Denoises each training sweep with cross-validated Savitzky–Golay filtering, then interpolates across stimulus amplitude using several passive-regime models: local voltage and conductance interpolation, shape-preserving interpolation, monotonic interpolation, and constrained/unconstrained low-order polynomials. Leave-one-amplitude-out validation is performed only on the two interior training amplitudes, preserving whole sweeps; the best smoothing/hyperparameter setting per model family is retained and the strongest families are validation-weighted. This avoids using test labels while exploiting both temporal smoothness and the expected near-linear, mildly nonlinear current–voltage relationship.

chart_rows.baseline_name: Conventional task baseline
Conventional task baseline
chart_rows.description: This method models the cell's passive voltage response as a linear, time-invariant (LTI) system, justified by the sweep-aligned, subthreshold experimental regime, negative-only input amplitudes, and constant step inputs. The code estimates the cell's impulse response (finite impulse response kernel) using the four training sweeps, via ordinary least squares solution to the multichannel convolution equation: input current predicts voltage deflection. This learned filter is then convolved with each of the two held-out test steps to predict their voltage responses. The kernel length (impulse response duration) is chosen by cross-validation on training sweeps (leave-one-out RMSE), with an upper bound of 100 ms (50 samples) to avoid overfitting slow drifts. No nonlinearity, regularization, or feature engineering is used: this is interpolation of subthreshold, time-aligned, baseline-subtracted traces. Predictions are clipped to be finite and precisely match test_x shape. The code is fully deterministic and suitable for single-run evaluation.

chart_rows.baseline_name: Conventional task baseline
chart_rows.description: Deterministic passive interpolation using a time-varying linear gain estimated from training sweeps. For each time sample t, we fit a zero-intercept ordinary least-squares slope g(t) between voltage deflection and injected current across the four training amplitudes: g(t) = sum_j x_j(t)*y_j(t) / sum_j x_j(t)^2. This yields the step response shape per unit current. We then smooth g(t) with a short symmetric Hamming window, calibrate its steady-state scale to match the slope estimated from the last 20% of samples (preserving the correct resistance), and enforce physical constraints (non-negativity, monotonic increase via cumulative maximum, and g(0)=0). Predictions for the two held-out sweeps are obtained by pointwise multiplication y_pred(t) = g_hat(t) * x_test(t). No test labels are used; rows are treated independently; only linear passive interpolation within a single cell is assumed. The method is vectorized, uses no randomness, and returns finite outputs with the same shape as test_x.

This fit_predict implementation creates a non-causal (acausal) single-trial regression model mapping observed neurons to held-out neurons, leveraging temporal and cross-neuron context within each trial while not using data from other trials for smoothing. The approach is as follows: (1) For each time bin, form a per-trial feature vector by stacking all held-in (observed) neuron counts at all 35 time bins (flattened as a feature vector of size 35x107). The decoder predicts the expected spike count of each held-out neuron at each time bin, using as input the activity of all held-in neurons over the entire time course of the trial. (2) A separate Ridge regression is fit independently for each held-out neuron and each time bin. (3) The regressors are trained on the 99 training trials only, without any data leakage between trials, and predictions are made for each trial independently, producing nonnegative expected counts per bin. (4) Negative predictions (impossible as expected spike counts) are thresholded to zero. This model makes full use of within-trial temporal context (whole-trial regression), but does not transfer smoothing or features across trials. All computations use NumPy and sklearn's Ridge regression (L2 regularization, deterministic random_state).

Multi-output ridge regression on log-counts with within-trial acausal temporal context. We model the expected spike counts of 35 held-out neurons from 107 observed neurons using a linear readout applied to lagged features of the observed population. Steps: (1) log1p-transform observed and target counts; (2) build a symmetric within-trial temporal window of observed activity (±5 bins, zero-padded at trial edges so no information crosses trial boundaries); (3) flatten trials×time to a design matrix; (4) select the ridge regularization strength via 5-fold GroupKFold cross-validation over trials to avoid leakage across the same trial; (5) fit a single multi-target Ridge to predict log1p(targets) from standardized lagged features; (6) predict on test, invert with expm1, clip to nonnegative finite counts. Offline acausal context is only within the same trial, no joining/smoothing across trials. Outputs are expected counts per 20 ms bin with shape (100, 35, 35), finite and nonnegative. Deterministic seed is set.

chart_rows.baseline_name: ZAPBench NLinear architecture, analytical fixed-ridge1 local reproduction
chart_rows.description:
Analytic NLinear-style forecaster with training-only fitting and per-horizon shrinkage.
- Pool every neuron and window: for each (example, neuron), form a 64-D history vector and a 32-D target.
- Subtract the last observed frame from both history and target to learn future deltas.
- Fit a shared temporal affine map (64→32) with ridge regularization (alpha=1.0) and an unpenalized bias using closed-form normal equations on training data only.
- Calibrate a per-horizon shrinkage factor gamma (size 32) by least-squares mixing against the naive "repeat last frame" baseline, clipped to [0,1] for stability.
- Predict on test: subtract last frame, apply the affine map, shrink deltas by gamma, and add the last frame back. If any numerical issue occurs, fall back to repeating the last input frame.
- Deterministic, NumPy-only, vectorized across all neurons and windows; returns finite outputs with shape (len(test_x), 32, 256).

chart_rows.baseline_name: Conventional task baseline
chart_rows.description: Aggregates repeated presentations by exact image, then fits spatially regularized log-link Poisson encoding models to the per-image mean counts. Orthonormal 2-D DCT features impose candidate smooth receptive-field priors; an SVD removes unidentifiable directions. Five-fold validation is grouped by unique image, evaluates Poisson loss separately for each neuron, and conservatively selects among regularization/smoothness settings and a constant-rate model. Models are refit on all unique training images. Test images are deduplicated before prediction so every repeat receives exactly the same positive expected 300 ms count.

chart_rows.baseline_name: Conventional task baseline
chart_rows.description: Fits spatially smoothed linear and quadratic count models with exponential or softplus links. Pools repeated training images, uses image-grouped cross-validation for neuron-specific regularization and ensemble weights, and returns identical positive expected counts for identical test images.

chart_rows.baseline_name: Conventional task baseline
Conventional task baseline
chart_rows.description: We implement a regularized linear Poisson encoding model for image-driven spike counts. Each neuron is fit independently using Poisson regression (generalized linear model with log link), regularized via L2 (ridge) penalty to prevent overfitting given high-dimensional image features. To identify an appropriate regularization strength per neuron, we use 3-fold cross-validation on the training set, optimizing the mean Poisson negative log-likelihood. Predictions on the test set are computed as expected spike counts (per 300 ms) for each unique image in the test set. Identical test images (repeats) are recognized and assigned consistent rates by hashing image vectors. The final output shape is (900, 41), positive and finite, as required. All code is deterministic and uses only allowed libraries (numpy, sklearn).

chart_rows.baseline_name: Conventional task baseline
chart_rows.description: Deterministic per-neuron Poisson GLM with L2 (ridge) regularization. Features (18x18=324) are standardized once using train set mean/std. For each neuron, alpha (regularization strength) is selected by 3-fold cross-validation over a small log-spaced grid using primary objective (Poisson negative log-likelihood). The final model for each neuron is refit on all training data with the chosen alpha. Predictions for test are computed only as a function of image features; identical test images are deduplicated so their predicted rates are identical. Outputs are positive expected spike counts per 300 ms. Implementation uses sklearn.linear_model.PoissonRegressor when available, otherwise falls back to TweedieRegressor(power=1, link='log'). Randomness is fixed for reproducibility. No use of test target labels or trial indices; no external models.

chart_rows.description: This solution uses a regularized linear regression (Ridge) to predict two-dimensional monkey finger velocities from 96-dimensional causal filtered spike count features. The approach is motivated by the high sample count, linearity assumptions in similar neuroprosthetic decoding regimes, and the need to mitigate overfitting and account for cross-day neural variability via chronologically-aware validation. The regularization parameter (alpha) is selected by grid-searching a few candidate values using Ridge regression and time-series split: the training set is split chronologically into 5 sequential folds, each preserving trial/session boundaries. We select the model with the highest mean variance-weighted R2 (calculated according to the main metric) across validation folds. The chosen model is retrained on the whole training set and used to predict on test data. No normalization or fitting occurs on test data per rules, and all operations are completed in a deterministic and memory-efficient manner.

chart_rows.baseline_name: Conventional task baseline

chart_rows.description: This solution implements a classical EEG epoch decoding approach using time-domain feature extraction suitable for sensor-space EEG with physically-referenced electrodes and minimal prior information. Inspired by common spatial pattern (CSP)-like approaches but without specialist libraries, the pipeline extracts log-variance features from manually-selected central-motor electrodes known to respond to hand motor imagery (C3, C4, CZ). For each trial, the log-variance is computed from short, overlapping windows in these channels. Additionally, mean, standard deviation, and band power features in the mu (8-13 Hz) and beta (13-30 Hz) bands are computed for all channels using SciPy's FFT. Channels are processed independently and concatenated to form a compact but rich trial feature vector. All feature extraction uses only training data to avoid leakage. A logistic regression classifier is trained using balanced class weights for robustness against potential label imbalance, and Scikit-learn's StratifiedKFold cross-validation is used to select the regularization strength in a leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) fashion (subject IDs are not provided, so LOSO is approximated with 5-fold stratified splits). No data from test subjects is used in any training step. The final model predicts the test set in a single pass. All NumPy/SciPy/sklearn operations use deterministic seeds; no external packages are used. The approach is designed for balanced accuracy scoring and robust, generalizable performance across held-out test subjects.

Filter-bank CSP with LDA for cross-subject motor imagery decoding. We use three physiologically motivated bands (8–12, 12–18, 18–26 Hz) and compute per-band Common Spatial Patterns (CSP) with small covariance shrinkage, extracting 3 pairs (6 comps) per band and using log-normalized component variances as features. Additionally, we compute lateralization features: per-band log-power differences for four symmetric channel pairs (C3–C4, CP3–CP4, FC3–FC4, C1–C2) to capture contralateral mu/beta desynchronization robustly across subjects. Signals are zero-phase Butterworth band-pass filtered. Features from all bands are concatenated, z-scored on the training set, and classified with shrinkage LDA (solver='lsqr', shrinkage='auto'). Deterministic seed and fixed hyperparameters are used; no test labels or calibration are used and no within-test adaptation is performed. Primary metric is balanced accuracy; no cross-validation is run to avoid overfitting and to maintain speed.

chart_rows.description: Subject-balanced, artifact-limited ERP classifier. It averages each channel into 31.25 ms bins over 94–906 ms, then combines a shrinkage-LDA model on all channel–time features with a supervised eight-component xDAWN-like spatial projection. Five deterministic subject-held-out folds select covariance shrinkages and the blend weight by mean per-person ROC-AUC. Spatial filters, moments, covariance references, and final models are fitted exclusively from training people; test trials are transformed independently without adaptation or boundary inference.

Ensembles shrinkage LDA on averaged EEG waveforms, epoch-normalized waveforms, and xDAWN covariance tangent features. Regularization and ensemble weights use three-fold person-held-out validation with equally weighted person ROC-AUC. All fitted transforms are refitted using training people only; test trials are processed independently.

This method implements a cross-person EEG P300 target detection using a linear ensemble classifier. 1) Preprocessing: Each trial is z-scored channel-wise using statistics computed from training data only. 2) Feature extraction: Temporal windows are selected based on typical P300 latency (e.g., mean signal in 300–600ms after flash), and means are extracted per channel. 3) A channel-wise linear discriminant analysis (LDA) classifier is trained and combined into a meta-LDA. Regularization is selected using Leave-One-Group-Out (LOGO) cross-validation across training people, validating generalization to new people. The trained classifier is then applied to test trials after the same preprocessing and feature steps, returning one score per test trial. Calibration or threshold fitting is not performed on test data or across person boundaries.

Approach: learn a cross-subject linear spatio‑temporal discriminator of P300 by using only training people for all fitting and validation.

Pipeline
- Feature extraction per trial (train/test):
  - Temporal smoothing with a short centered moving average (edge-padded, zero‑phase by symmetry) to reduce noise.
  - Temporal binning (mean over non-overlapping bins) with decimation factor 4 (128 Hz → 32 time bins in 1 s) to obtain compact ERP features.
  - Flatten time×channel features; no use of any test data statistics.
- Standardization: per-feature z‑score using training data only (and fold‑specific training data during CV), with safe std floor.
- Classifier: L2‑regularized Logistic Regression (liblinear, class_weight='balanced', deterministic seed). Scores are decision_function values (higher ⇒ more likely target) and are not probability-calibrated.

Validation/tuning using training people only
- Use subject-held-out GroupKFold with 5 splits (groups=train_groups).
- Grid over temporal smoothing length L in {1,5} samples and logistic C in {0.5,1.0,2.0} (decimation fixed at 4).
- For each candidate, gather cross-validated predictions so each person is evaluated exactly once; compute ROC-AUC per person and report the mean across persons equally (skip persons with a single class, though that should not occur here).
- Refit the chosen configuration on the full training data and score the test set.

Notes
- No transforms fitted on test inputs; no test grouping inferred; no transductive steps. Deterministic behavior with fixed seed. Runtime/memory kept modest by compact features (16 channels × 32 time bins = 512 dims) and a small grid.

chart_rows.description: Extracts robust per-epoch EEG features (multiband FFT powers, spectral ratios, amplitude/difference statistics, autocorrelation and Hjorth-style measures), adds unsupervised per-night robust normalization, acausal rolling context, and fixed clock-time features. It fits a class-balanced Extra Trees/Histogram Gradient Boosting ensemble. Leave-one-night-out training predictions select the ensemble mixture, modest class-probability corrections, and transition-smoothing strength using fixed-class macro-F1. Final sequence decoding uses train-label transition associations, never crosses night boundaries, and ignores -1 labels during fitting and transition estimation.

Extracts EEG spectral, waveform, and acausal temporal features with robust per-night normalization. Uses gradient boosting with leave-one-person-out probability features and a temporal second-stage classifier. Training-only out-of-fold predictions select mild Markov smoothing and class adjustments for macro F1. Unknown training labels are excluded from fitting; night boundaries are preserved. No test labels or pretrained assets are used.

chart_rows.description: This solution performs classification of sleep EEG epochs into five sleep stages (Wake, N1, N2, N3, REM) using feature-based machine learning. For each night, it normalizes the raw EEG per night (z-score), extracts signal and spectral features from each epoch (such as power in delta/theta/alpha/sigma/beta bands, zero-crossing rate, and signal variance), and uses a RandomForestClassifier (scikit-learn) trained only on labeled epochs (y != -1) from five training individuals. It uses stratified validation splits by night during training to tune hyperparameters and avoid overfitting to individual sleep patterns. The classifier learns on all training nights jointly, but always preserves night boundaries and does NOT treat the sleep data as a single continuous stream. For prediction, it applies the same per-night normalization and feature extraction on the three test nights and predicts labels for all epochs. The output follows the required shape. The code uses numpy, scipy, and sklearn, and is self-contained without any external dependencies.

chart_rows.description: EEG sleep staging with compact spectral/time-domain features, per-night unsupervised normalization, multinomial logistic regression, and HMM-style temporal decoding. For each night we: (1) detrend each epoch by mean, (2) extract vectorized features: time-domain (std, peak-to-peak, mean absolute value, line length, zero-crossing rate, Hjorth mobility/complexity, skewness, kurtosis), frequency-domain via rFFT with Hamming window (relative bandpowers in delta/theta/alpha/sigma/beta for 0.5–30 Hz, three log band ratios, spectral centroid, spectral entropy, SEF90), and time-of-night features (index, sin, cos). Features are z-scored per night (unsupervised adaptation). We train a multinomial LogisticRegression (class_weight='balanced') on all labeled epochs (ignoring -1). A 5x5 Markov transition matrix and initial distribution are estimated from labeled training sequences with Laplace smoothing and diagonal self-bias. Test emissions are classifier probabilities mapped into 5 classes (missing classes get tiny mass). We decode each test night offline with Viterbi, then apply a light de-islanding pass to replace 1-epoch flips. Nights are processed independently, preserving boundaries. Deterministic seeds, single-thread classifiers, and no external assets.

chart_rows.baseline_name: Conventional task baseline
Conventional task baseline
chart_rows.description:
This solution repairs ocular (EOG) artifacts in EEG segments using a supervised regression approach with frequency-wise Wiener filtering, leveraging the matched pairs of noisy (mixture) and clean EEG segments. The core concept is that ocular artifacts are stereotyped, broadly low-frequency, and their mixing is linear, so learned linear spectral-domain filtering is a practical approach. All segments are one channel, standardized per segment, with 512 samples (2 seconds at 256 Hz). The algorithm proceeds as follows: 

1. Both train_x (mixture) and train_y (matched clean EEG) are transformed with the real FFT (rFFT) along the time axis per segment, yielding frequency coefficients.
2. For each frequency bin, a linear regression model (Ridge regression, =0.05 for robustness to collinearity and noise) is fit from the noisy train_x rFFT coefficient to the clean train_y rFFT coefficient.
3. For each held-out noisy segment in test_x, rFFT is applied, frequency-wise denoised coefficients are predicted using the learned regression weights, and the inverse rFFT reconstructs the time-domain denoised segment.
4. Output shape matches test_x.

This method handles both amplitude and phase adjustments per frequency, robustly attenuates linear ocular artifacts, and internalizes the normalization regime of the data. Ridge regression (rather than OLS) helps avoid overfitting or instability due to the semi-synthetic mixing. The method uses no external weights nor specialist packages. All inference and reconstruction is vectorized for efficiency; only numpy and sklearn (for Ridge) are used. No information about test target labels is used, in accord with standard offline artifact removal expectations.

chart_rows.baseline_name: Conventional task baseline
chart_rows.description: Denoising is learned as a single-channel, zero-phase, frequency-domain Wiener filter estimated from the training set. For each segment we compute an rFFT; across all training segments we estimate, per frequency bin, the linear least-squares transfer H(f) that maps the mixture X(f) to the clean target Y(f): H = sum_i conj(X_i) Y_i / (sum_i |X_i|^2 + λ). Because both mixture and clean are normalized by the mixture’s per-segment standard deviation, the ratio is invariant to that scaling and approximates S_cc/(S_cc+S_aa). We constrain H to be real (zero-phase), clamp it to [0,1], and smooth it across frequency to reduce variance. Hyperparameters (λ relative Tikhonov, smoothing window length, and a small shrinkage toward identity) are chosen by a small deterministic 80/20 hold-out split to minimize average per-segment relative RMSE on the validation fold. With the best hyperparameters, H is re-estimated on all training data and applied to test segments via rFFT -> multiply by H -> irFFT. The result has the same shape as test_x. This is computationally light, deterministic, and respects the per-segment standardization noted in the context.

chart_rows.baseline_name: Conventional task baseline
chart_rows.description: Deterministic subject-held-out ensemble. It builds three independent trial-level feature views: raw optical-density dynamics with fixed temporal projections, within-trial spatially centered dynamics, and homologous left/right-hemisphere contrasts based on the symmetric channel ordering. Each candidate uses train-fold robust scaling, clipping, univariate feature selection, and a class-balanced linear classifier. chart_rows.baseline_name: Conventional task baseline
chart_rows.description: Deterministic linear decoder with train-only preprocessing and small CV for hyperparameters. Steps: (1) Build features per trial from optical-density (OD) data shaped (136 channels, 8 bins). chart_rows.description: Train-only robust ensemble for cross-cohort IQM classification. Acquisition-geometry and voxel-count fields are excluded to reduce scanner/protocol confounding. Within each fit, nonfinite values are median-imputed, robustly scaled, clipped using training-fold statistics, and accompanied by missingness indicators. A class-balanced random forest, class-balanced extremely randomized trees model, and regularized class-balanced logistic model are combined with fixed weights. A deterministic stratified 5-fold out-of-fold ensemble selects the decision threshold that maximizes balanced accuracy, after which models are refit on all training scans. Test data are transformed only with full-training statistics; no test-distribution statistics or test labels are used.

Train-only median imputation and robust scaling, with relative tissue-intensity features and acquisition-grid/count features removed to reduce cohort shortcuts. Four-fold stratified training validation selects and weights balanced logistic regression, RBF SVM, random forest, and extra-trees models, then sets a conservative balanced-accuracy threshold. No test labels or test-distribution statistics are used; all selected models are refit on the full training set.

chart_rows.baseline_name: Imputed balanced RandomForest500; fixed hyperparameters

chart_rows.description: This solution builds a binary classifier to determine MRI scan acceptability based on precomputed image quality metrics (IQMs). The approach uses a pipeline with (1) train-set-only median imputation for missing values, (2) train-set-only robust scaling (median/IQR), and (3) a balanced random forest classifier (class_weight='balanced', random_state fixed, 100 trees). Cross-validation is used internally on the training set (stratified 5-fold, balanced accuracy scoring) to grid-search both max_depth and min_samples_leaf hyperparameters. No information from the test set is used beyond applying the fitted imputer/scaler. Test data is not used for statistics or model tuning. Integer predictions (0=include, 1=exclude) are returned with shape (n_test,). No identifiers, site, or label fields are used. All IQMs are treated as numeric. No tuning based on test outcomes is performed. This is a straightforward single-model solution maximizing generalizability with careful handling of missing data and class imbalance.

Binary IQM-based MRI QC classifier for ABIDE→DS030 generalization. Pipeline: (1) replace ±inf with NaN; (2) train-only per-feature median imputation; (3) append missingness indicators (one per original feature); (4) train-only standardization (mean 0, std 1; zero-std features left unscaled). Classifier ensemble: RandomForestClassifier (class_weight='balanced_subsample', depth-limited) + LogisticRegression (L2, class_weight='balanced'). A 5-fold stratified CV on ABIDE yields out-of-fold probabilities for both models; we grid-search a convex blending weight α∈[0,1] and a decision threshold τ∈[0.05,0.95] to maximize balanced accuracy on OOF predictions. Final models are refit on all training data, test probabilities are blended with the chosen α, and labels are produced using τ. Deterministic seed (42); RandomForest n_jobs=1. Only training-derived statistics are used for imputation and scaling; no test labels are used. Predictions are integer labels with shape (n_test,).

Final label IDs are distinct for each test image. No pixels outside valid geometric test extent are labeled. The output is a (2,727,546) numpy array of labeled images for both test images. latest_successes.description: Learns a global intensity threshold and an object scale from annotated training patches, then performs seeded instance segmentation on each test image independently. Training uses only pixels within the valid ROI (channel1==1) and ignores unknown labels (train_y<0). The global threshold is chosen by maximizing pixel-wise F1 on a coarse grid across evenly subsampled training patches. Object scale is estimated as the median GT instance area; from this we derive a seed separation (local-max window) and a mild Gaussian smoothing sigma. For each test image: (1) smooth intensity; (2) threshold to a foreground mask inside geometric extent (channel1>0.5); (3) detect local maxima above a stricter peak level (peak_rel=max(thr+0.1, thr*1.15), clipped to 0.95) with non-maximum suppression window based on learned scale; (4) ensure at least one seed per connected foreground component by adding the brightest pixel if needed; (5) assign every foreground pixel to its nearest seed via an EDT-based Voronoi within the mask (watershed-equivalent over distance to seeds); (6) remove instances with area<4 pixels and relabel consecutively. Pixels outside the test extent mask are set to background 0. Each test image is processed separately; no attempt is made to reconcile labels across images or patches. Deterministic, single-thread friendly, uses only numpy/scipy.

latest_successes.description: This method segments puncta in fluorescence microscopy images using classical image processing and machine learning based feature learning. Workflow: (1) For training, each 128x128 patch is featurized with pixel intensities, geometric coordinates (normalized xy), local gradients, and simple multi-scale shape-texture statistics. Only labeled regions (channel1 == 1) and valid pixels (train_y >= 0) are used. For each labeled object in a patch, we extract centroid locations and create instance-specific foreground masks. A RandomForestClassifier is trained to predict background vs punctum center. A per-training-patch global threshold is grid-searched to maximize foreground F1>0.5 under synthetic instance separation (patch-wise local IDs), using only annotated pixels. At test time, each whole test image is split into 128x128 overlapping windows (step 64). Per-pixel features are extracted and pixels are classified. Patch probabilities are averaged at overlaps. Pixelwise probability map is then thresholded and postprocessed: (a) valid extent mask applied; (b) small holes and objects <4 px are removed; (c) watershed with local maxima as seeds separates instances. Final label IDs are distinct for each test image. No pixels outside valid geometric test extent are labeled. The output is a (2,727,546) numpy array of labeled images for both test images. All computation is strictly local to individual images; no smoothing/config leakage/correlation across source fields or samples. Deterministic result due to fixed seed. No specialized packages or pretrained weights are used.
latest_successes.patch_description: Retain the original 30-tree depth-9 random forest, features, training fields, seed, one CPU thread, threshold grid and inference. Cap each tree bootstrap at 250000 draws from all eligible training pixels (instead of 16451616), chosen before test scoring after training-only profiling located the time bottleneck. This changes the fitting budget and potentially predictions; it is a manual budget adaptation, not an exact compatibility fix or an untouched GPT-4.1 score. Also pass signed int32 watershed markers as required by SciPy; confirmed by a synthetic-array compatibility probe and the preserved r3 runtime error. This avoids unsigned 8-bit label truncation.

chart_rows.description: A deterministic, leakage-safe soft-voting ensemble. Conventional task baseline
chart_rows.description: This implementation predicts independent expert morphology labels (0: aspiny, 1: spiny) from 11 electrophysiology features per cell, with possible NaNs. The task requires donor-generalizing predictions: no overlap between train and test donors. To maximize macro-F1 and balanced accuracy, it preprocesses features using robust median imputation (to avoid train/test leakage), then standardizes with RobustScaler (median and IQR) fitted on training data. For classification, a deterministic RandomForestClassifier with class_weight='balanced' is used to mitigate class imbalance and provide non-linear decision boundaries. 5-fold (StratifiedKFold) CV is run on training data to set the best max_depth (macro-F1), restricted to a grid [3,5,7,9,13,17,21] as a compromise between expressiveness and overfitting risk (due to donor split). A deterministic (seeded) model is used. The final model with this hyperparameter is then fitted to all training data and used for test prediction. All pipeline steps (imputation, scaling, classifier) are composed in a sklearn Pipeline for robust and easy transformation. Predictions for the test set are returned as a 1D numpy array of integers of length n_test. No file/network I/O or external dependencies are used.

chart_rows.baseline_name: Conventional task baseline
chart_rows.description: Deterministic, donor-disjoint-ready classifier for spiny/aspiny morphology from 11 electrophysiological features. Training-time preprocessing is applied only on training folds. The method builds an equal-weight ensemble of four complementary models: (1) logistic regression on standardized, median-imputed features with missing-value indicators; (2) HistGradientBoosting (handles NaNs natively; falls back to GradientBoosting + imputation if HGB is unavailable), fit with class-balanced sample weights; (3) RandomForest with class_weight balanced and imputation; (4) ExtraTrees with class_weight balanced and imputation. We perform 5-fold StratifiedKFold to generate out-of-fold (OOF) ensemble probabilities for the training set: for each fold, every base model is fit on the fold’s training split (preprocessing fitted only on that split), produces validation probabilities, and also predicts the test set. Within each fold, base probabilities are averaged to form the fold-ensemble probability. OOF ensemble probabilities are concatenated to cover all training rows; test ensemble probabilities are averaged across folds. A single decision threshold is chosen by maximizing macro-F1 on the OOF ensemble probabilities (balanced accuracy is used as a tie-breaker, with preference toward thresholds close to 0.5 if still tied). The final test labels are obtained by applying this threshold to the averaged test ensemble probabilities. Seeds are fixed for reproducibility and all tree models use n_jobs=1 to comply with single-thread constraints.

chart_rows.description: Deterministic primal linear-SVM classifier with fixed per-spot summary features and training-only standardization. Three regularization values and fixed class-prior margin adjustments are selected by leave-one-donor-out validation, averaging fixed seven-label macro-F1 across the two held-out donors. Square-root inverse-frequency weights reduce imbalance; absent fold classes are explicitly aligned without failure. The selected model is refit on all training donors, with no test-set normalization or adaptation.

Use leave-one-training-donor-out validation with all seven labels fixed in macro-F1. Select a probability ensemble of regularized linear, discriminant, logistic, and approximate RBF models. Fit preprocessing within each validation fold, then refit selected models on all training spots. Test predictions use independent per-row calculations only.

This solution assigns human cortical-layer labels from SRT spot expression using a robust supervised approach suitable for donor-held-out cross-validation and full section transfer. First, it standardizes training and test data using robust per-gene normalization fit on training alone (Median+MAD). To handle highly skewed class count imbalances and donor/section variation, the model exploits a stratified GroupKFold inner-validation using the donor IDs in train_groups. For model selection, we combine a multinomial logistic regression (multi-class, one-vs-rest, balanced class weights) and a RandomForestClassifier (100 trees, max_depth=15). Their predicted class probabilities are weighted and averaged for each spot, providing smooth probabilistic outputs even when some labels are missing in individual validation folds. Prediction is performed by fitting both models on the full training set and averaging their test predicted probabilities. If a label was never observed in a training fold, its probability is set to zero and probabilities are renormalized, ensuring the output always covers all 7 layers (as required for test sections). The 7-class predictions are output as integer indices 0..6, one per test row. All feature transforms and model hyperparameters are strictly fit on training data only; gene order is preserved throughout. NumPy's random seed is fixed for consistency. No features, normalization, or adaptation use test data or image context, and the workflow adheres to all contest/data constraints.

Training-mouse-stratified3fold selection among standardized/imputed RBF SVM and ExtraTrees, using primary grouped metric; no verified SOTA claim
chart_rows.description: This implementation solves the specified task—mouse-disjoint optotagged PV/SST waveform classification—using a rigorous, neuroscience-appropriate cross-validation and pipeline selection scheme. It precisely heeds grouping and class balance for validation, never using leak-prone test or biological info for training processes. Preprocessing uses median imputation and standardization on training data only. Two model types (RBF SVM and ExtraTrees) are compared using three-fold, mouse-stratified cross-validation, strictly via the provided cv_fold vector and using only the provided mouse IDs for grouping. Within the given computational constraints and deterministic seeding, it selects the best CV performer and predicts labels for the held-out test set. The solution is complete, self-contained, and consistent with the provided context.

chart_rows.baseline_name: Training-mouse-stratified3fold selection among standardized/imputed RBF SVM and ExtraTrees, using primary grouped metric; no verified SOTA claim
chart_rows.description: Mouse-disjoint PV/SST classifier with fixed inner CV model selection. The procedure: (1) build candidates: RBF SVM with C in {0.1,1,10,100} using median imputation + standardization, and ExtraTrees (500 trees, max_features in {sqrt,1}) using median imputation only; all with deterministic seed 20261031 and one numerical CPU thread where applicable. (2) Use the provided three-fold cv_fold to run mouse-disjoint validation. Each fold fits preprocessing on its training partition only. (3) Optimize by the primary class_balanced_mouse_accuracy: accuracy is computed per mouse, averaged across mice within PV and SST separately, then averaged across the two classes. (4) During each fit, derive sample weights from training data only so that every mouse contributes equally within its class and each class sums to equal total weight: for each class, each mouse gets total weight 1/num_mice_in_class, uniformly distributed over its cells. (5) Refit the chosen model on all training data with the same preprocessing and weighting, then predict test labels. Output is a finite integer numpy array of shape (71,) with labels 0=PV, 1=SST. Only training data determine all transforms; group_ids and cv_fold are used solely for CV and weight construction; no test identifiers are used; single-threaded trees; deterministic outcomes.

chart_rows.baseline_name: Quadratic position×direction PoissonGLM, fixedtinyL2
chart_rows.description: Chronologically blocked model selection with one-second gaps. The estimator compares regularized Poisson spline models (position-only, additive position/velocity, and position–velocity interactions) with occupancy-normalized smoothed position tuning curves, including direction-sensitive variants. Complexity and shrinkage toward the training mean are selected using two forward validation blocks; the strongest configurations are refit on all training data and averaged. Outputs are finite nonnegative expected spike counts per 20 ms bin.

chart_rows.baseline_name: Quadratic position×direction PoissonGLM, fixedtinyL2
chart_rows.description: Ensemble of smooth Poisson models for position, direction-dependent place fields, and position–velocity interactions. Weights use two chronological validation blocks with 1-second buffers; models are then refitted on all training data. Returns expected spike counts per 20-ms bin.

chart_rows.baseline_name: Quadratic position×direction PoissonGLM, fixedtinyL2
Quadratic position×direction PoissonGLM, fixedtinyL2
chart_rows.description: This function fits a Poisson regression model using a flexible, nonlinear mapping from behavior (position, velocity) to expected spike counts, suitable for a single neuron where counts per 20ms bin are small and nonnegative. The approach uses regression splines (cubic) for each behavioral covariate to allow for nonlinearities, then fits a (regularized) generalized linear model with Poisson loss. The model is trained only on training data in temporal order (no shuffling, no cross-bin validation). The predicted rate per bin is multiplied by 0.02 to account for the 20ms bin size, ensuring predictions are expected counts per bin. No external specialized packages or non-allowed imports are used; only numpy and sklearn's Ridge regression (for stable fitting) are utilized. The code guarantees nonnegative, finite predictions for each test bin and matches the prescribed output shape.

chart_rows.baseline_name: Quadratic position×direction PoissonGLM, fixedtinyL2
chart_rows.description: Poisson generalized linear model with nonlinear feature expansion. We construct a compact, smooth encoding of firing as a function of position and movement speed. Features include: (a) third-order polynomials of position, velocity, and absolute speed; (b) Gaussian radial basis functions (RBFs) over position; (c) Gaussian RBFs over absolute speed; and (d) multiplicative interactions between position-RBFs and speed-RBFs to capture position-by-speed modulation. Feature columns are standardized using training statistics. We fit a PoissonRegressor (log link, L2 penalty) and select the regularization strength alpha by a strictly chronological split of the provided training segment (first 80% for fitting, last 20% for validation), maximizing validation Poisson log-likelihood (ignoring the constant log-factorial term). The final model is refit on the full training segment with the chosen alpha and used to predict expected spike counts per 20 ms bin on the test segment. No spike history or test labels are used, and time order is preserved throughout. Predictions are nonnegative expected counts per bin (not Hz).

chart_rows.description: Laplace-preconditioned Hamiltonian Monte Carlo for ten distinct logistic-GLM posteriors. Each observation gets its own MAP/Hessian whitening transform and independently evolved chain. The sampler uses exact supplied full prior precision, Metropolis correction, randomized trajectory lengths, 1,200 warm-up iterations, dual-averaging step-size tuning for the first 900 iterations, and deterministic per-observation RNG streams derived from the seed. Draw order is deterministically shuffled after sampling; no diagonal approximation is imposed.

Metropolis-corrected Hamiltonian Monte Carlo samples each observation’s separate joint posterior using the full supplied precision matrix. Four chains per observation use MAP curvature, covariance adaptation, and step-size tuning toward 90% acceptance during 950 warm-up transitions, followed by 100 fixed-tuning burn-in transitions. Three transitions separate retained draws; all sampling is seeded.

This implementation samples from the posterior of a ten-parameter Bernoulli GLM for ten independent observations. For each, we use elliptical slice sampling (ESS), a robust Markov chain Monte Carlo method for non-conjugate posteriors with zero-mean Gaussian priors with known precision Q. Each chain draws 10,000 posterior samples of the parameter vector (beta), skipping the first 2,000 as burn-in, with deterministic PRNG splitting per observation. Likelihood, gradient, and log-density computations use efficient numpy vectorization to ensure fast iteration. The code handles the full covariance of the prior without assuming independence. No external or specialist packages are used. The output shape is (10, 10000, 10): ten per-observation posteriors, each of 10,000 draws, dimension 10.

Ten separate posteriors are sampled for a 10-parameter Bernoulli-GLM with a shared stimulus design matrix and Gaussian prior N(0, Q^{-1}). For each observation (row of spike_trains), we first find the MAP by Newton’s method on the exact log posterior and compute the Laplace curvature H = X^T W X + Q at the mode (W = diag(sigma*(1-sigma))). The inverse H^{-1} is used as a fixed preconditioning (mass) matrix for a Metropolis-Adjusted Langevin Algorithm (MALA). Proposals are preconditioned: beta' = beta + 0.5 * eps^2 * H^{-1} grad(beta) + eps * L z, with L the Cholesky of H^{-1}, and the MH correction uses the exact asymmetric Gaussian proposal densities. The log posterior and gradient are evaluated exactly at both current and proposed states. The step size eps is adapted during burn-in via a Robbins–Monro update on log eps to target an average acceptance rate of about 0.57, then frozen. Burn-in defaults to max(600, min(1200, n_samples//8)). After burn-in, exactly n_samples draws are returned per observation. This approach captures joint covariance and dependence while keeping computation fast (small p, n=100). RNG is deterministic via the provided seed. Output shape is (10, n_samples, 10) with finite float64 values.

chart_rows.description: Uses deterministic five-fold mouse-held-out validation with equal total weight per mouse. It fits a diverse ensemble of regularized logistic, histogram-gradient-boosting, and extra-trees models on behaviorally structured stimulus/history features; out-of-fold equal-mouse log-loss determines a nonnegative blend and conservative calibration. All supervised fitting and scaling use training mice only, after which models are refit on all training data.

Fits regularized stimulus/history logistic models and shallow gradient boosting. Deterministic four-fold mouse-disjoint validation selects a probability mixture using equal-mouse log loss; training also weights mice equally. Refits on all training mice and returns finite choice probabilities.

Fit a regularized logistic regression using sklearn, treating each mouse as a group for cross-validation hyperparameter selection. Only training mice (IDs) are used for fitting and hyperparameter tuning (via GroupKFold cross-validation). Categorical history features (choices, feedbacks) are numerically encoded as provided. Data is standardized on train only, including contrasts and block prior, using means/stds from training mice. The best C (inverse regularization strength) is chosen by mouse-disjoint log-loss. Predict turnCW probability for each test example (from test-only mice), with deterministic RNG for reproducibility. All code fits in <240 lines, uses only allowed numpy, scipy, and sklearn, and does not reference any session info or joining. Probabilities are clipped to [1e-6,1-1e-6] as per scoring protocol. The design fairly estimates generalization to new mice by exclusively holding test-mouse data separate throughout all model selection and fitting.

Model: L2-regularized logistic regression trained only on training mice with group-aware cross-validation and per-mouse equalization. Features include sensory evidence (right/left contrasts), experimenter block prior (and its logit), their interactions, and history terms from the last five choices/feedbacks plus reinforcement-like products and recency-weighted aggregates. All transforms are fitted on training data only; no identifiers or ordering are used. Hyperparameter C is chosen by 5-fold GroupKFold on mouse IDs, optimizing the primary metric: mean negative log-likelihood averaged per validation mouse. Fitting uses sample weights that make each training mouse contribute equally. Final probabilities on test are clipped to [1e-6, 1-1e-6], representing P(turn CW = source choice +1) per test row.

chart_rows.description: Fits the exact conditional choice likelihood for each agent on a dense bounded alpha–beta grid and returns marginal posterior medians under uniform priors. Posterior medians regularize weakly identified finite-sample cases while directly targeting absolute parameter error.

Fits the conditional Q-learning likelihood and returns marginal posterior medians under uniform priors over the allowed ranges. Deterministic numerical integration accounts for finite-sample uncertainty and weak parameter identifiability.
Independent dense quadrature with Simpson marginalization and trapezoid-CDF inversion; uniform priors over prompt bounds. Post-hoc audit, not the frozen primary MLE reference.

This code estimates the Q-learning parameters (alpha: learning rate, beta: inverse temperature) for each independent agent based on their choice and reward history. The fitting is done via maximum likelihood estimation, explicitly simulating the Q-learning process per parameter candidate. The code uses bounded optimization (L-BFGS-B) with multiple restarts for each agent to minimize the negative log-likelihood, carefully handling the initialization and constraints. The final result is a (N,2) ndarray of agent-wise (alpha, beta) estimates.

Estimate per-agent learning rate (alpha) and inverse temperature (beta) for a two-action Q-learning model by maximum likelihood. For each agent, we compute a coarse grid search over alpha and beta to find good starting points, then refine using L-BFGS-B under bounds alpha in [0.01, 0.99] and beta in [0.1, 10]. The likelihood is computed with stable log-sigmoid math, updating only the chosen action’s Q with observed rewards. Missing trials (NaN or invalid choices/rewards) are skipped for both likelihood and learning updates. Returns an (N,2) array with [alpha, beta] for each agent.

chart_rows.description: Inspects legacy and newer NWB layouts, identifies the six sweep pairs, verifies sampling rates, and computes pulse timing and voltage statistics using stored physical-unit conversions.

This function extracts metadata and quantitative measurements for sweeps 19–24 from an NWB file. It programmatically locates acquisition response and stimulus TimeSeries for each sweep, determines sampling rates, units, and conversion factors, computes sample counts and dt. It loads and scales each stimulus and response signal, identifies the main hyperpolarizing (negative going) current step relative to stimulus holding median (using a -1e-6 pA threshold for at least one sample and selecting the longest such run), extracts main pulse onset/duration, then computes main pulse amplitude, pre-stimulus voltage (50ms before pulse), and mean voltage deflection during the pulse—all with unit conversions as required (pA for current, mV for voltage). It decodes all relevant string or byte-string attributes robustly, and supports legacy as well as modern NWB storage patterns.

Reads an NWB/HDF5 file with h5py, locates stimulus and response TimeSeries for sweeps 19–24, computes sampling and signal metrics, and returns the required JSON-serializable structure. The implementation is robust to NWB1/NWB2 layout variations by scanning for TimeSeries under /stimulus and /acquisition, uses dataset conversion/offset attributes, decodes stored units, converts to pA/mV for computations, detects the main negative pulse as the longest contiguous run below the median by ≥1e-6 pA, and computes onset/duration/amplitude and voltage deflection using sample-count windows. Only the specified file is read; no external files or tools are used.

latest_successes.superiority_reason: Manual debugging after observed failure; final usability only, not fresh model capability.
latest_successes.description: This function extracts metadata and quantitative measurements for sweeps 19–24 from an NWB file. It programmatically locates acquisition response and stimulus TimeSeries for each sweep, determines sampling rates, units, and conversion factors, computes sample counts and dt. It loads and scales each stimulus and response signal, identifies the main hyperpolarizing (negative going) current step relative to stimulus holding median (using a -1e-6 pA threshold for at least one sample and selecting the longest such run), extracts main pulse onset/duration, then computes main pulse amplitude, pre-stimulus voltage (50ms before pulse), and mean voltage deflection during the pulse—all with unit conversions as required (pA for current, mV for voltage). It decodes all relevant string or byte-string attributes robustly, and supports legacy as well as modern NWB storage patterns.

latest_successes.description: Reads an NWB/HDF5 file with h5py, locates stimulus and response TimeSeries for sweeps 19–24, computes sampling and signal metrics, and returns the required JSON-serializable structure. The implementation is robust to NWB1/NWB2 layout variations by scanning for TimeSeries under /stimulus and /acquisition, uses dataset conversion/offset attributes, decodes stored units, converts to pA/mV for computations, detects the main negative pulse as the longest contiguous run below the median by ≥1e-6 pA, and computes onset/duration/amplitude and voltage deflection using sample-count windows. Only the specified file is read; no external files or tools are used.
latest_successes.patch_description: Classify time-series groups by the visit path (including stimulus/acquisition hard-link aliases), rather than a resolved object name. Preserve the returned schema and extraction algorithm. Traverse stimulus and acquisition aliases independently with ancestor-cycle protection; visititems skips previously visited hard-linked objects. Parse actual supplied-file metadata, never expected answers. Normalize visit paths to absolute form before prefix classification. Mechanical AST-identical physical-line formatting; original format violation remains historical.
